title: Streamline audit ingest: tiered storage, index rotation, and cost controls
creator: Asha Mehta
description:
Problem: Our current audit logging ingestion writes all events into a single hot index group which drives high storage costs, slow index lifetime operations, and long tail query latency for historical investigations. Additionally, retention and cold-tiering are configured inconsistently across orgs.

Goal: Build a robust ingestion and storage lifecycle for audit logs that: (1) partitions by org+day for query isolation and efficient deletion, (2) enforces a multi-tier storage lifecycle with automatic cold tiering and archival, (3) supports fast indexing and low write latency under bursty ingestion, and (4) exposes cost controls and visibility per-customer. This ticket scopes the design and the initial implementation for the ingestion pipeline, indexing strategy, retention automation, and operational dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: Ingestion writes to time-and-org-partitioned indices (audit-<org>-YYYY.MM.DD) with transparent routing
Index lifecycle policies implemented: hot -> warm -> cold -> delete/archive according to per-org retention policy
Automatic daily index roll and safe reindex path for schema evolution
Storage cost shows measurable reduction (target: 30% decrease in S3/equivalent tiering costs for audit retention after 90 days) in the org-level cost dashboard
Backpressure and retry behavior documented and tested under 2x peak ingestion rate
Operational runbook added and alerting configured (ingest lag, failed bulk requests, disk pressure, retention job failures)
implementation_notes: Routing: add org_id header from API layer; ingestion service will hash and write to audit-<org>-YYYY.MM.DD index with daily alias for reads
Compression: enable LZ4/GZIP on bulk ingestion and prefer columnar-friendly JSON->NDJSON streaming to reduce RAM and network overhead
Index mappings: use explicit typed fields for common audit attributes (actor_id, action, resource_type, outcome, timestamp) and store raw_event for full payload
Partitioning: keep daily indices for first 30 days, then roll to weekly indices between 31-180 days, then monthly for older retention windows to reduce shard count
Lifecycle policies: implement ILM or equivalent to move segments to cold storage (S3 IA/Glacier) with searchable freeze where supported; create safe snapshot-based archival for compliance export
Querying: provide daily aliases audit-<org>-current for low-latency reads and audit-<org>-all for full-history searches; recommend query filters on timestamp+org for performance
Schema evolution: write consumer that validates incoming event version and routes incompatible events to quarantined index with metric and PR for backward-compatibility migration
Cost controls: per-org retention policy flag, budget cap flag (auto-summarize oldest indices when over budget), and admin console UI hooks (separate PR)
rollout_plan: Week 1: Implement index naming, routing header, and daily roll logic in ingestion service behind feature flag
Week 2: Deploy ILM/policy automation to staging and run synthetic load test at 3x production ingest
Week 3: Add cold-tier snapshot logic and validate restore workflows with compliance team
Week 4: Gradual canary: enable for 5 low-traffic orgs, monitor alerts and cost metrics
Week 5: Ramp to 25% orgs, add admin UI hooks for retention per org
Week 6: Full rollout, update runbooks, run incident tabletop with SRE and security
testing_plan: Synthetic load test at 2x and 3x peak with randomized event size distributions
End-to-end restore test from cold snapshots for a 90-day retention window
Query latency regression suite comparing current single-index baseline vs partitioned indices
Chaos test: simulate ES node failure and validate ILM/recovery behavior
